title: Differential Susceptibility of hiPSC-Derived Neural Progenitors and Neurons to Measles Virus Infection Reveals Unique Neuronal Budding and Viral Mutations
abstract: Abstract Measles virus (MeV) can cause severe neurological complications such as measles inclusion body encephalitis (MIBE) and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), but the mechanisms of MeV infection in the human Central Nervous System (CNS) remain poorly understood. In this study, we modeled MeV infection in the CNS using neural progenitor cells (NPC) and cortical neurons derived from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC), evaluating infectivity, viral replication and mutation, and neural function after infection. NPC were highly susceptible and permissive to infection, forming cytoplasmic inclusion bodies, undergoing apoptotic death, but producing infectious particles. In contrast, neurons supported viral replication but did not produce infectious progeny, despite the visualization of budding viral particles by Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Our findings advance the understanding of MeV neuropathogenesis and support the utility of hiPSC-derived neural models for studying neurotropic viral infections since we could reproduce key aspects of MeV neuronal infection.

title_zh: hiPSC来源的神经前体细胞和神经元对麻疹病毒感染的差异易感性揭示了独特的神经元芽生和病毒突变
source_body_en: Abstract Measles virus (MeV) can cause severe neurological complications such as measles inclusion body encephalitis (MIBE) and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), but the mechanisms of MeV infection in the human Central Nervous System (CNS) remain poorly understood. In this study, we modeled MeV infection in the CNS using neural progenitor cells (NPC) and cortical neurons derived from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC), evaluating infectivity, viral replication and mutation, and neural function after infection. NPC were highly susceptible and permissive to infection, forming cytoplasmic inclusion bodies, undergoing apoptotic death, but producing infectious particles. In contrast, neurons supported viral replication but did not produce infectious progeny, despite the visualization of budding viral particles by Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Our findings advance the understanding of MeV neuropathogenesis and support the utility of hiPSC-derived neural models for studying neurotropic viral infections since we could reproduce key aspects of MeV neuronal infection.
abstract_zh: 摘要 麻疹病毒(MeV)可引起严重的神经并发症,如麻疹包涵体脑炎(MIBE)和亚急性硬化性全脑炎(SSPE),但MeV在人类中枢神经系统(CNS)中的感染机制仍不明确。在本研究中,我们利用人类诱导多能干细胞(hiPSC)来源的神经前体细胞(NPC)和皮层神经元模拟MeV在CNS中的感染,评估感染后的感染性、病毒复制和突变以及神经功能。NPC对感染表现出高度易感性和允许性,形成细胞质包涵体,经历凋亡死亡,但能产生感染性颗粒。相比之下,神经元支持病毒复制,但未产生感染性子代,尽管通过传播电子显微镜(TEM)观察到了芽生病毒颗粒。我们的研究结果推进了对MeV神经发病机制的理解,并支持使用hiPSC来源的神经模型来研究神经嗜性病毒感染,因为我们能够再现MeV神经元感染的关键特征。

title: Outcome of Measles in Vaccinated versus Unvaccinated Children under 5 years of age
abstract: Objective: To determine the frequency of measles vaccination among children under 5 years of age presenting with measles and to compare the outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated children. Outcomes were defined as (i) prolonged hospital admission of two days or more (primary outcome, taken as the marker of severe disease) and (ii) measles-related complications (secondary outcome). Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Paediatrics, Benazir Bhutto Hospital, Rawalpindi, from October 2025 to December 2025, and reported in accordance with the STROBE guidelines for cross-sectional studies. A total of 150 children aged 1–5 years of either sex were enrolled using non-probability consecutive sampling. Measles was defined by the WHO clinical case definition (fever ≥38 °C with a generalised maculopapular rash lasting ≥3 days, together with at least one of cough, coryza, or conjunctivitis). A child was classified as vaccinated when at least one dose of a measles-containing vaccine given at or after 9 months of age was documented on the Expanded Program on Immunisation (EPI) card, and as unvaccinated when no dose was documented. Children with chickenpox, other skin infections, congenital anomalies, chronic illnesses, immunocompromised status, or incomplete vaccination records were excluded. Groups were compared using the chi-square test, and effect sizes were reported as odds ratios (OR), risk ratios (RR), and absolute risk differences with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: The mean age of the children was 3.18 ± 1.21 years, and the mean weight was 12.46 ± 2.84 kg. Of the 150 children, 38 (25.3%) were vaccinated, and 112 (74.7%) were unvaccinated. Prolonged hospital admission was required by 57 of 112 (50.9%) unvaccinated children compared with 10 of 38 (26.3%) vaccinated children (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.29–6.53; RR 1.93, 95% CI 1.10–3.39; absolute risk difference 24.6%, 95% CI 7.8–41.4; p = 0.009). Complications were observed in 73 (48.7%) children overall, with pneumonia being the most common complication in 34 (22.7%), followed by diarrhoea in 21 (14.0%), otitis media in 10 (6.7%), and encephalitis in 8 (5.3%). The overall frequency of complications did not differ significantly between unvaccinated (55/112, 49.1%) and vaccinated (18/38, 47.4%) children (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.51–2.24; p = 0.853). Conclusion: Unvaccinated children < 5 years of age with measles had a significantly greater need for prolonged hospital admission than vaccinated children, indicating that measles vaccination attenuates the severity of illness in children who acquire the infection. The overall frequency of complications did not differ significantly between the two groups; this null result should be interpreted cautiously, given the small number of vaccinated children and the correspondingly wide confidence interval. These findings support the need to strengthen routine measles immunisation coverage in children under 5 years of age. Keywords: Measles; Measles Vaccine; Vaccination; Child, Preschool; Hospitalization; Treatment Outcome; Immunization Programs; Pakistan.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the outcomes of measles in vaccinated versus unvaccinated children under 5 years of age. It aimed to compare the frequency of measles vaccination and its impact on disease severity. Conducted at Benazir Bhutto Hospital in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, from October to December 2025, the descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 150 children using non-probability consecutive sampling. Measles was defined by the WHO clinical case definition, and vaccination status was determined by EPI card records. Results showed that 25.3% of children were vaccinated, while 74.7% were unvaccinated. Prolonged hospital admission was significantly more common in unvaccinated children (50.9% vs. 26.3%), with an odds ratio of 2.90 and a p-value of 0.009. However, the overall frequency of complications did not differ significantly between the groups. The study concluded that measles vaccination reduces the severity of illness in children who acquire the infection, supporting the need to enhance immunisation coverage. The findings are limited by the small number of vaccinated children and wide confidence intervals, which may affect the interpretation of complication rates.

title: Measles Risk and MMR Vaccination Timing in Dermatology Patients on Immunosuppressive Therapy
abstract: The 2025-6 measles outbreak marked a significant resurgence of a vaccine-preventable disease, raising urgent public health concerns. The clinical implications of this outbreak for patients on immunosuppressive therapy, specifically in dermatology, remains poorly defined. This review addresses this gap, examining measles presentations and complications in immunosuppressed dermatology patients. We discuss diagnostic considerations specific to this population, in whom impaired humoral immunity can limited the reliability of standard testing. Finally, we propose a practical, dosing and pharmokinetic-based framework for MMR vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis decisions across commonly used dermatologic therapies. This includes specifically biologics, targeted small molecules, and conventional immunosuppressants. Current public health guidance was largely developed from oncology, transplant, and rheumatology populations, leaving dermatologists without a clear or actionable plan for their patients. This review is intended to fill that gap and serve as a quick reference tool for dermatologists navigating measles risk in the context of immunomodulatory therapy.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒),历史名称如麻疹和麻疹病,以及相关疾病如亚急性硬化性全脑炎。核心问题是皮肤病患者在接受免疫抑制治疗时面临麻疹的风险,以及该人群在MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防方面的最佳时机。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述基于2025-6 麻疹 暴发,探讨了免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。它讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,并强调了皮肤科医生缺乏明确公共卫生指导的现状。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,麻疹对接受免疫抑制治疗的皮肤病患者构成重大风险,由于体液免疫受损,标准诊断检测的可靠性可能受限。它强调了需要为疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防制定个性化的策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,目前针对麻疹预防的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,导致皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。这代表了在免疫抑制治疗皮肤病患者中特定证据的空白。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了一个基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。其目标是为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。

abstract_zh: 2025-6 麻疹 暴发标志着一种疫苗可预防疾病的显著回升,引发了紧迫的公共卫生关注。这种暴发对接受免疫抑制治疗的患者,特别是在皮肤病患者中,其临床意义尚未明确。本综述旨在填补这一空白,探讨免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。我们讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,其中由于体液免疫受损,标准检测的可靠性可能受限。最后,我们提出了一种基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。这包括特定的生物制剂、靶向小分子药物以及传统免疫抑制剂。目前的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,使得皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。本综述旨在填补这一空白,并为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。

title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case
abstract: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.
journal: CAUCHY: Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

title: Nationwide Surveillance and Control Measures during Large Measles Outbreak, Bangladesh, 2026
abstract: Nationwide surveillance in Bangladesh during April 2-May 27, 2026, identified a total of 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed measles cases across 8 administrative divisions. Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Despite high reported vaccine coverage, transmission persisted amid residual immunity gaps. Vaccine stockouts, discontinued vaccination campaigns, and coverage overestimation likely contributed to Bangladesh's largest recorded measles outbreak.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of nationwide surveillance and control measures during a large measles outbreak in Bangladesh, 2026, and to identify factors contributing to the persistence of transmission despite high vaccine coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted nationwide surveillance in Bangladesh from April 2 to May 27, 2026, across 8 administrative divisions, identifying 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed measles cases.
analysis.methods: The study relied on reported data from surveillance systems and public health records to assess the outbreak's scale, identify contributing factors, and evaluate the effectiveness of control measures.
analysis.main_results: Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Transmission continued despite high reported vaccine coverage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the challenges in measles control, even with high vaccine coverage, and suggest that vaccine stockouts, discontinued campaigns, and coverage overestimation may have played a significant role in the outbreak.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for improved vaccine distribution, sustained vaccination campaigns, and accurate coverage monitoring to prevent future outbreaks and reduce measles-related mortality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by reliance on reported data, which may be subject to underreporting or inaccuracies, and the lack of direct laboratory confirmation for all cases. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the nationwide measles outbreak in Bangladesh during April 2 to May 27, 2026, identifying 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed cases. Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Despite high reported vaccine coverage, transmission persisted, likely due to vaccine stockouts, discontinued campaigns, and coverage overestimation. The findings emphasize the importance of reliable vaccine distribution and continuous surveillance to prevent future outbreaks. The study's reliance on reported data introduces potential limitations, reducing the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估2026年孟加拉国大规模麻疹暴发期间全国范围内的监测及控制措施的影响,并确定尽管疫苗覆盖率较高,传播仍持续存在的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在2026年4月2日至5月27日间,对孟加拉国8个行政区域进行了全国范围的监测,发现了67,079例疑似病例和8,834例确诊病例。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究依赖于监测系统和公共卫生记录中报告的数据,以评估暴发的规模、确定相关因素,并评估控制措施的有效性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在疑似病例中报告了472例死亡,在确诊病例中报告了88例死亡。尽管报告的疫苗覆盖率较高,传播仍持续存在。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了在麻疹防控中面临的挑战,即使具有高疫苗覆盖率,也表明疫苗短缺、中止的活动以及覆盖率高估可能在暴发中发挥了重要作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了改进疫苗分发、持续疫苗接种活动以及准确监测覆盖率的必要性,以防止未来的暴发并减少与麻疹相关的死亡率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于依赖报告数据,这些数据可能存在低估或不准确的情况,且所有病例均未进行直接实验室确认。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在2026年4月2日至5月27日间,对孟加拉国8个行政区域进行了全国范围的监测,发现了67,079例疑似病例和8,834例确诊病例。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究依赖于监测系统和公共卫生记录中报告的数据,以评估暴发的规模、确定相关因素,并评估控制措施的有效性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在疑似病例中报告了472例死亡,在确诊病例中报告了88例死亡。尽管报告的疫苗覆盖率较高,传播仍持续存在。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了在麻疹防控中面临的挑战,即使具有高疫苗覆盖率,也表明疫苗短缺、中止的活动以及覆盖率高估可能在暴发中发挥了重要作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了改进疫苗分发、持续疫苗接种活动以及准确监测覆盖率的必要性,以防止未来的暴发并减少与麻疹相关的死亡率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于依赖报告数据,这些数据可能存在低估或不准确的情况,且所有病例均未进行直接实验室确认。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FAMILY SUPPORT AND MEASLES VACCINE PROVISION TO CHILDREN
abstract: Measles remains a contagious disease that contributes to high rates of child morbidity and mortality in Indonesia, while measles vaccine coverage in several regions has not yet reached the national target. Low vaccination coverage is influenced by various factors, one of which is family support in child health decision-making. This study aims to analyze the relationship between family support and measles vaccine administration in children in the Karang Penang Community Health Center (Puskesmas Karang Penang) working area. The study used a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional correlational design. The study population was all mothers or caregivers of children targeted for measles immunization, totaling 36 respondents, using a total sampling technique. Data collection was conducted using a closed questionnaire regarding family support and measles vaccine status. Data analysis used the Chi-Square test to determine the relationship between variables. The results showed that most respondents had good family support and the majority of children had received the measles vaccine. Statistical tests showed a significant relationship between family support and measles vaccine administration in children with a p-value of 0.001 (p<0.05). This study demonstrates that family support plays a crucial role in increasing measles immunization compliance, thus providing the basis for developing family-based immunization education and service strategies to improve child health and prevent measles transmission.

title: Schedule-stage divergence between DTP3 and first-dose measles-containing vaccine coverage in selected Western Balkan countries
abstract: To compare childhood vaccination coverage in Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia and assess divergence between DTP3 and later measles-containing vaccine coverage during 2019-2023. Material and methods. A retrospective comparative ecological time-trend study used WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for DTP3, MCV1, and MCV2. Annual trends, change from the 2019 baseline to the lowest value in 2020-2021, subsequent change to 2023, and the DTP3-MCV1 difference were described. The DTP3-MCV1 difference was defined as an ecological indicator of divergence between early infant-series vaccination and later measles-vaccination contact, not as an individual dropout measure. No inferential modeling was performed because only five annual observations per indicator were available. Albania maintained DTP3 coverage at 97% in 2023, while its DTP3-MCV1 difference widened from 4 to 14 percentage points. Montenegro had persistently low coverage across the selected indicators and a 57-point DTP3-MCV1 difference in 2023. North Macedonia narrowed this difference from 17 to 13 points, while Serbia narrowed it from 10 to 9 points and returned MCV2 to its 2019 value. No country reached at least 95% for both measles doses in 2023. DTP3 and MCV1 followed different country-level patterns during 2019-2023. Albania maintained high DTP3 coverage but showed widening DTP3-MCV1 divergence, whereas North Macedonia and Serbia showed partial narrowing, and Montenegro retained a very wide difference. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; the DTP3-MCV1 comparison is ecological and should not be interpreted as individual dropout, continuity, or causality.

title: A Retrospective Multicenter Study of Measles Seropositivity in Korea from 2014 to 2024
abstract: Background: Measles is a highly contagious viral disease requiring high herd immunity.Although the Republic of Korea has maintained measles elimination through national immunization programs, sporadic cases continue to occur.We evaluated age-and period-specific measles immunity levels using laboratory-based measles antibody data from Korea.Methods: In this retrospective multicenter seroepidemiological study, measles IgG and IgM test results obtained at eight medical institutions in Korea between January 2014 and September 2024 were analyzed.Seropositivity was analyzed by year, age group, sex, and region.Associations between demographic factors and antibody positivity were assessed using Poisson regression, and differences across assay platforms were analyzed using negative binomial regression.Results: A total of 383,441 measles IgG and 36,879 IgM tests were included.IgG seropositivity was 56.9-68.2%during 2014-2018, increased to 87.8% in 2019, and remained high at 87.2-88.2%during 2020-2024.The proportion of equivocal IgG results decreased from 14.2-17.9%during 2014-2018 to 3.0% in 2019 and remained low thereafter.IgM seropositivity was 2.5-7.2%during 2014-2018, decreased to 1.3% in 2019, and remained low at 0.5-1.0%during 2020-2024.The proportion of equivocal IgM results also declined over time.IgG seropositivity was lower among children and adolescents and highest among adults aged 50-69 years, whereas IgM seropositivity was relatively higher in younger age groups.Regional and assay platform-related differences were observed.Conclusions: Measles seropositivity patterns in Korea showed heterogeneity by age, region, and assay platform.Standardized interpretation considering assay characteristics may improve post-elimination measles surveillance.

title: Modeling The Impact of Public Enlightenment on Measles Transmission Dynamic in Kafin Hausa Metropolitan
abstract: Measles is a very contagious illness with symptoms such as fever, rash, cough and redness of eyes. It can cause very dangerous consequences such as brain infection and pneumonia. In this research work, SIR model was formulated in order to assess the effect of public enlightenment on the transmission dynamics of measles infection in Kafin Hausa metropolis of Jigawa state. In the mathematical analysis section, the existence, boundedness, and positivity of the solution have been established. The existence of the disease equilibria indicates that there exist two equilibria for the model. They are disease-free equilibrium (DFE) and disease endemic equilibrium point (DEEP). It was determined that the DFE is locally asymptotically stable when the effective reproduction number is less than one (R 1). The numerical simulation reveals that, the public enlightenment rate on Atypically and Severe exposed individuals is the important parameter to reduce the dynamics transmission of measles disease in Kafin Hausa metropolitan, Jigawa State.

title: Comparative Analysis of Classical, Fractional, and Quantum Calculus Models for Measles Transmission Dynamics
abstract: This study presents three mathematical models of measles transmission that utilize pulse vaccination strategies: classical ordinary differential equations, Caputo fractional derivatives, and Jackson q-derivatives. The basic reproduction number R0 has been derived, and the global stability of equilibria has been investigated using an SIRS model with bilinear incidence. The quantum calculus model facilitates the integration of discrete-pulse vaccination strategies by applying geometric time scales. The existence, uniqueness, positivity, and global asymptotic stability of equilibria have been demonstrated through Lyapunov’s direct method. Numerical results indicate that while equilibria remain model-independent, transient dynamics exhibit significant variation. The fractional-derivative models reduce epidemic peaks by up to 5.6%, whereas the quantum-calculus model results in an increase of 1.1%. These models provide essential tools for enhancing pulse vaccination strategies in measles elimination initiatives.

title: Perceive Severity of Measles Resulting into the Uptake of Second Dose Measles Vaccine (MCV2) Among Caregivers of Under-Five Children in Bauchi North, Bauchi State
abstract: Measles is a serious public health issue particularly in developing nations with high tolls of morbidity and mortality among children coupled with low immunization uptake. Despite global efforts to eliminate measles through widespread immunization programmes, its outbreaks continue to occur due to gaps in vaccine coverage. In Nigeria, measles is one of the leading causes of vaccine-preventable deaths among children of under-five years old. So, assessing the perceived severity of measles resulting into the uptake of the second dose of measles vaccine among caregivers of under-five children is crucial for designing effective interventions to improve vaccination coverage. In this cross-sectional study, a total of 403 caregivers were selected using multistage sampling technique. A researcher-developed questionnaire was used in collecting data which was analysed using SPSS version 26 and the result was presented in frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations and a one sample t-test of inferential statistics was used to test the postulated hypothesis. The finding revealed that the observed t-value (159.67) is greater than the critical t-tabulated value (1.649) at 0.05 level of significance. This shows that caregivers perceive the severity of measles significantly influences the uptake of MCV2. It was concluded that perceived severity of measles resulting into the uptake of MCV2 among caregivers of under-five children in Bauchi north is significant. In view of this, enhancing caregivers understanding and awareness of the severity and complications of measles, addressing misconceptions about vaccine safety and the protection that the MCV2 vaccine provides through comprehensive community mobilization and sensitisation campaigns by involving religious and traditional leaders of the communities was recommended to improve vaccination coverage.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF HEALTH AND PHARMACEUTICAL RESEARCH

title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies
abstract: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May. This article analyses the public health response to the outbreak and evaluates the government's management of the crisis. Health professionals and measles experts have attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

title: ĐÁNH GIÁ CHẤT LƯỢNG VÀ ĐỘ ỔN ĐỊNH CỦA VẮC XIN SỞI VÀ VẮC XIN PHỐI HỢP SỞI–RUBELLA SẢN XUẤT TẠI POLYVAC TRONG GIAI ĐOẠN 2020–2026 ASSESSMENT OF THE QUALITY AND STABILITY OF THE COMBINED MEASLES–RUBELLA VACCINE MANUFACTURED AT POLYVAC, 2020–2026
abstract: Đặt vấn đề: Vắc xin phối hợp Sởi–Rubella (MRVAC) do POLYVAC sản xuất giữ vai trò quan trọng trong tiêm chủng mở rộng tại Việt Nam. Việc kiểm soát chất lượng và đánh giá độ ổn định theo tiêu chuẩn WHO-GMP là điều kiện tiên quyết nhằm khẳng định tính an toàn và hiệu quả ổn định, nhất quán của vắc xin. Mục tiêu: Đánh giá chất lượng, tính nhất quán vắc xin MRVAC (2020–2026) và tác động của cải tiến công nghệ sản xuất bán thành phẩm lên chất lượng và độ ổn định của vắc xin thành phẩm. Phương pháp: Phân tích dữ liệu kiểm nghiệm 49 lô thành phẩm (2020–2026) theo các chỉ tiêu hiệu giá, độ ổn định nhiệt (37°C/7 ngày), lý hóa, vô trùng và an toàn. Theo dõi độ ổn định dài hạn (2–8°C) và lão hóa cấp tốc (25°C, 37°C) trên các lô đại diện cải tiến; so sánh thống kê trước và sau thay đổi. Kết quả: 100% lô thành phẩm đạt tiêu chuẩn chất lượng. Hiệu giá Sởi đạt 4,40 ± 0,09 lg PFU/0,5 ml (CV = 2,07%), với độ giảm hiệu giá ở 37°C/7 ngày là 0,86 ± 0,07 lg PFU/0,5 ml; ). Hiệu giá Rubella đạt 3,81 ± 0,08 lg PFU/0,5 ml (CV = 1,99%) với độ giảm hiệu giá là 0,06 ± 0,03 lg PFU/0,5 ml. Các chỉ tiêu hóa lý, an toàn đạt tiêu chuẩn với biến thiên rất thấp. Các lô sau cải tiến duy trì độ ổn định dài hạn tương đương lô trước, đạt chất lượng đến 24 tháng (2–8°C), 90 ngày (25°C) và 11 ngày (37°C) và không ghi nhận xu hướng chất lượng bất thường. Hiệu giá Sởi đạt 4,40 ± 0,09 lg PFU/0,5 ml (CV = 2,07%), với độ giảm hiệu giá ở 37°C/7 ngày là 0,86 ± 0,07 lg PFU/0,5 ml; ). title: Association of gut microbiota and regulatory T cells with vaccine immunogenicity in HIV-exposed uninfected and HIV-unexposed infants: a longitudinal cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Responses to vaccines reflect the functionality of the immune system. We measured BCG, tetanus and measles vaccine responses in HIV-exposed uninfected (HEU) and HIV-unexposed (HUU) infants to identify factors associated with HEU immunologic defects. METHODS: We assessed cell-mediated immunity (CMI) by FluoroSpot, antibodies by ELISA, regulatory and immunologic checkpoint inhibitor-expressing T cells (Tregs/Ticis) by flow cytometry, and gut microbiota by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. CMI and antibody responses were the primary outcome measures. Associations with Tregs/Ticis and gut microbiome parameters were identified using the hurdle model, Spearman correlations and enrichment analyses. FINDINGS: Among 123 HEUs and 117 HUUs, HEUs tended to have lower BCG-CMI than HUUs without reaching statistical significance (p = 0.07) and similar tetanus-CMI, measles-CMI, and measles-antibodies. Multiple Treg and Tici subsets had significant or marginal negative effects on CMI (p = 0.003-0.10). Treg/Tici inclusion in the hurdle model decreased the statistical significance of the negative effect of HEU status on BCG-CMI suggesting that Tregs/Ticis may have contributed to the difference between HEUs and HUUs. Enrichment of the gut microbiota in Actinobacteria and Firmicutes was significantly associated with low vaccine immunogenicity (p = 0.002-0.04), and Bacteroidetes and Proteobacteria with high immunogenicity (p < 0.0001-0.10). The Firmicute Murdochiella sp. had a higher negative effect size on BCG-CMI in HEUs than HUUs (p < 0.0001). High microbiome diversity negatively correlated with CMI responses (p = 0.002-0.03), with higher effect sizes in HEUs than HUUs (p = 0.047). INTERPRETATION: The frequency of Tregs/Ticis and the composition of the gut microbiome are associated with immune responses to vaccines and may contribute to decreased responses in HEUs. The internally consistent association between the enrichment of gut microbiota in specific phyla and the immunogenicity of several vaccines suggests the possibility of designing mitigating interventions that target the gut microbiome. FUNDING: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases and Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, National Institutes of Health.

title: A Bayesian adaptive shift-mixture approach for estimating incubation period and exposure time in small outbreaks
abstract: Rapid estimation of infection time and the incubation-period distribution is essential for evidence-based quarantine and contact tracing. However, outbreak data typically mix primary and higher-generation cases with unobserved exposure times. We propose the infection-induced adaptive shifted-knots Dirichlet process mixture (IASK-DPM) model, a nonparametric Bayesian framework applying a Dirichlet process prior on the shift parameter in a three-parameter lognormal kernel. Incorporating infectious dynamics, the base measure is derived from a kernel-density estimate of observed onset times, concentrating mixture components where the epidemic curve is dense while preserving support in the left tail, where earlier exposure may plausibly lie. The proposed framework is intended primarily for small-outbreak or early-phase epidemic settings in which infections are concentrated around a limited number of dominant transmission episodes or narrow exposure windows. Posterior inference uses Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and is implemented in R/Stan . In nine Monte Carlo scenarios representing COVID-19, measles, and O-157 outbreaks, IASK-DPM reduced mean squared error in shift parameter estimates (i.e. exposure time) by 35% to 70% and in the 95th incubation percentile by 30% to 68%, relative to fixed finite-mixture models. These gains persisted even when the competing Dirichlet-process model used a conventional base measure. Applied to the 2015 Korean MERS outbreak, the method recovered four exposure dates (4.7–19.5 days after May 10, 2015), coinciding with field-investigated superspreading events, and estimated a posterior median incubation of 5.8 days (95th percentile 13.7 days), aligning with exhaustive contact tracing. By allowing the data, rather than the analyst, to determine latent exposure generations, IASK-DPM enables accurate inference on key epidemic parameters with minimal tuning.

title: Vaccines, the Gut-Brain Axis, and Neurodevelopment: A Structured Narrative Review
abstract: Objective: To systematically evaluate the interface between vaccination and the gut-brain axis (GBA) in both directions of effect: first, whether vaccines or their components alter GBA biology, including microbiome composition, barrier integrity, cytokine responses, and mitochondrial function; second, whether pre-existing GBA state modifies the response to vaccination; and third, whether either direction bears on neurodevelopmental outcomes or on the adverse events recorded in trials and surveillance. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched directly, and the Walden University Library federated discovery service was used to search its subscribed collections, including MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, CINAHL, Scopus and ScienceDirect, from inception to 5 September 2025. Eligibility Criteria. Human and animal studies examining licensed vaccines or vaccine components with measurable outcomes in GBA domains, neurodevelopmental endpoints, or post-marketing adverse events. Of 3,047 records, 60 studies met inclusion criteria in the primary search, with a further 7 identified through a targeted supplementary search to September 2026, giving 67 included studies, listed in Appendix A. Microbiome composition influenced vaccine immunogenicity: higher Bifidobacterium abundance predicted stronger infant antibody responses, and neonatal antibiotic exposure reduced antibody titres to several infant vaccines measured at 7 months of age. Evidence on whether vaccination itself alters the microbiome is limited: one longitudinal adult cohort reported compositional stability, pediatric data are close to absent, and transient shifts have been observed in mice. Animal maternal immune activation models implicated IL-6 and IL-17A pathways in neurodevelopmental alterations, whereas maternal vaccination showed no such association. Cohorts exceeding one million children found no association between autism and the vaccine exposures they measured, principally measles-mumps-rubella vaccination, thimerosal and cumulative antigen count, consistent with a 2025 Danish cohort of aluminium-adsorbed vaccine exposure and a December 2025 WHO advisory reaffirmation. No study identified examined DTaP, hepatitis B or varicella in relation to neurodevelopmental outcomes. Few eligible studies directly assessed barrier or mitochondrial endpoints. Active surveillance quantified specific adverse events, including febrile seizures, intussusception, immune thrombocytopenic purpura, myocarditis (lower with 2023-2024 mRNA formulations), and anaphylaxis. The two directions of effect at this interface are supported to very different degrees, and that asymmetry is the principal finding. Evidence that gut microbiome state modifies vaccine response is moderate in certainty. Evidence on whether vaccination alters gut-brain axis biology, the direction the causal hypotheses in this field assert, is thin rather than negative: barrier, mitochondrial and paediatric data are essentially absent, and the single relevant longitudinal cohort concerns adults receiving COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. Large-scale epidemiology does not support vaccine-attributable increases in autism risk for the exposures those cohorts measured, principally measles-mumps-rubella vaccination, thimerosal and cumulative antigen count; it does not address the microbiome pathway. Several rare adverse events are quantifiable through active surveillance, whereas others remain uncertain signals. Continued active surveillance and transparent risk communication remain essential.

title: Potential Missed Vaccination Opportunities for Vaccine-Preventable Diseases Among Healthcare Workers
abstract: Objective: Vaccinating healthcare workers (HCWs) is a fundamental strategy to protect them from occupational exposure risks and the potential for transmission of infectious diseases to susceptible patients. This study aimed to evaluate HCWs’ vaccination status after periodic occupational health screenings in a tertiary healthcare facility, identify risk groups for pneumococcal disease, influenza, and hepatitis A, and determine potential missed vaccination opportunities. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed records of HCWs who underwent periodic occupational health screening at a tertiary healthcare facility between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2026. Only the most recent record was analyzed for HCWs with multiple screening records, resulting in a total of 775 HCWs being evaluated. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, serological status, and vaccination records were assessed. Risk groups for pneumococcal disease, influenza, and hepatitis A were identified based on current guidelines. A potential missed vaccination opportunity was defined as a situation in which an HCW had an indication for vaccination and presented to the occupational health unit, but the screening records contained no documentation that the vaccine had been recommended, administered, or declined. title: Combining CHARMM36m with OPC water improves accuracy
abstract: Abstract Atomistic simulations of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are notoriously sensitive to force field inaccuracies, either regarding the protein or the water model, yielding inaccurate observables such as compactness, secondary structure propensities, or kinetics. The currently most widely used IDP force fields are Amber99 sb -disp (A99disp) and C harmm 36m (C36m). A99disp includes a new water model and thus optimized both, the protein and the water interactions. In contrast, C36m used the T ip 3 p water model and optimized only protein interactions. In many cases, C36m+T ip 3 p underestimates radii of gyration compared to FRET or SAXS experiments. Such overly compact structural ensembles are believed to arise from an imbalance between protein-protein, protein-water, and water-water interactions, which might be due to T ip 3 p inaccuracies. Here, we aim at re-balancing these interactions by combining C36m with the Optimal Point Charge (OPC) water model. Recently, this C36m+OPC combination showed improved accuracy for the disordered domain of the measles virus nucleoprotein. Here we present a systematic assessment, comparing C36m+OPC, C36m+T ip 3 p , C36m+T ip 4 p , C22*, A03ws, A99 sb -ws, and A99disp for five IDPs, as well as a subset of those for five globular proteins, a set of disordered AGQ-repeat peptides, and the fast folding miniprotein CLN025. We compared extensive MD simulations ( > 8.5 ms) with SAXS, NMR, circular dichroism, photo-induced electron transfer (PET), T-jump infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray crystallography measurements. We found that combining C36m with OPC improved accuracy over C36m+T ip 3 p for IDP ensembles without compromising its accuracy for globular proteins. While also the kinetics of the AGQ-peptides were more accurate for C36m+OPC, those of CLN025 folding were less accurate. Overall, C36m+OPC showed similar accuracy as A99 sb -ws and A99disp, the latter is currently considered among the most accurate protein force fields.

title: Vaccination in Children with Paediatric Autoimmune and Autoinflammatory Rheumatic Diseases: Evidence on Safety, Immunogenicity and Effectiveness Across Live-Attenuated, mRNA and Recombinant Vaccines
abstract: Vaccination in children with paediatric autoimmune and autoinflammatory rheumatic diseases (pedAIIRDs) is clinically important but challenging. These children have an increased risk of infections due to both their underlying immune-mediated disease and the immunosuppressive therapies required for disease control. At the same time, immunosuppression may reduce vaccine-induced immune responses, while concerns about disease flares and the safety of live-attenuated vaccines may result in delayed or incomplete vaccination. This thesis aimed to generate clinically applicable, real-world evidence on the safety, immunogenicity and effectiveness of vaccination in children with pedAIIRDs receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Five studies addressed three vaccine platforms: the live-attenuated measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) booster vaccine, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and the recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix). In a cohort of 186 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), MMR booster vaccination was not associated with increased disease activity, including in children receiving biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, and no serious vaccine-related adverse events were observed. Long-term evaluation of 182 children with JIA showed that most patients maintained protective antibodies against measles, mumps and rubella. However, measles seroprotection five years after vaccination was significantly lower in patients receiving biologic therapy at vaccination than in those not receiving biologics, supporting a targeted approach to serological monitoring. A systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrated that COVID-19 vaccination was associated with a marked reduction in the risk of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). In a prospective cohort of 157 children with paediatric rheumatic diseases, COVID-19 mRNA vaccination induced humoral responses in nearly all patients and adequate T-cell responses in most tested patients. Although antibody concentrations were lower in patients receiving biologic therapy, vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic COVID-19 was preserved. No increase in disease activity, myocarditis or serious adverse events was identified. Finally, off-label use of RZV was evaluated in ten varicella-zoster-virus-naïve immunocompromised children for whom live-attenuated varicella vaccination was unsuitable. Nine of ten patients seroconverted following two doses. Two subsequently developed mild breakthrough varicella after household exposure and recovered without hospitalisation or antiviral treatment. Together, these studies support a shift from broad vaccine avoidance towards individualised, treatment-specific vaccination strategies in immunocompromised children. The findings provide evidence for the safe use of selected live vaccines, targeted monitoring of long-term vaccine-induced immunity, effective use of mRNA vaccines and further evaluation of non-live vaccine alternatives. These results may contribute to future national and international vaccination recommendations for children with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.

title: A cross-sectional study of womens’ knowledge and reported practices on reproductive, maternal and child health in rural area of North-Eastern India
abstract: Background: Women’s knowledge and health-seeking practices are crucial determinants of reproductive, maternal, and child health outcomes. Information from rural communities of North-Eastern India remains limited. The study aims to assess women’s knowledge and reported practices regarding reproductive, maternal, and child health and to determine the influence of sociodemographic factors on overall health knowledge. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 women selected from the rural field practice area of a tertiary care teaching hospital in Assam. Data were collected using a pretested interview schedule covering maternal and child health knowledge, preventive practices, and treatment-seeking behaviour. Health knowledge scores were generated based on correct responses. Univariate analysis was performed to summarize data, followed by multiple linear regression to identify factors associated with health knowledge. Results: Knowledge regarding diarrhoea prevention and management was poor; 52.3% had never heard of oral rehydration solution and only 20.7% recognized vaccination as a preventive measure against measles. Although 95% of women had received antenatal care, only 45.2% initiated breastfeeding within one hour of birth. Full immunization coverage was 65.7%. More than half (54.1%) sought initial treatment from ASHAs/ANMs. Higher educational attainment and increasing age were significantly associated with better health knowledge (P<0.05). Conclusions: Significant gaps exist in maternal and child health knowledge and practices among rural women. Educational status and age are important determinants of health knowledge, highlighting the need for targeted community-based health education interventions.

Although 95% of women had received antenatal care, only 45.2% initiated breastfeeding within one hour of birth. Full immunization coverage was 65.7%. Conclusions: Significant gaps exist in maternal and child health knowledge and practices among rural women. Educational status and age are important determinants of health knowledge, highlighting the need for targeted community-based health education interventions.

title: LIMD: LBP-InceptionV3 Hybrid Approach for Mpox Detection Using Skin Lesion Images
abstract: Mpox skin lesions may exhibit visual similarities with other infectious skin conditions, particularly chickenpox and measles, making reliable image-based differentiation challenging. This study presents an LBP InceptionV3 hybrid approach for Mpox detection using skin lesion images. The proposed framework combines high level visual representations extracted using pretrained InceptionV3 with complementary local texture information generated using Local Binary Pattern (LBP). The secondary dataset comprised 228 original images. 102 images belong to Mpox class, while 126 images belong to the others class (chickenpox and measles). The images were expanded through augmentation to 3,192 images comprising 1,428 Mpox and 1,764 Other images. Images were standardized to 224 × 224 pixels and divided into training, validation, and testing sets using a 70:15:15 ratio. InceptionV3 generated a 2,048-dimensional deep feature representation, while LBP texture maps were processed through a shallow convolutional network to obtain 512 texture features. The resulting 2,560-dimensional representation was fused for classification. The proposed model achieved 94.15% accuracy, 94.16% precision, 94.15% recall, 94.16% F1 score, and an AUC of 0.99. On the 479 image test set, 451 images were correctly classified, including 202 Mpox and 249 Other images. The ablation study demonstrated that incorporating LBP improved accuracy from 88.72% for InceptionV3 alone to 94.15%, representing a 5.43 percentage point improvement, while AUC increased from 0.95 to 0.99. In addition, clinically sourced images from Owerri General Hospital were used to provide an independent assessment of the model on previously unseen skin lesion samples. The findings demonstrate that combining deep visual and local texture representations provides an effective approach for Mpox skin lesion classification.
journal: American Journal of Neural Networks and Applications

title: An empirical study of CNN models and XAI for grape leaf disease detection based on data split ratios
abstract: The efficiency of deep learning (DL) models in detecting plant diseases is frequently evaluated on controlled datasets, with little attention paid to data-partitioning techniques that impact generalization in real-world scenarios. This study examines the effects of three data split ratios (80:10:10, 70:15:15, and 50:25:25) on the generalizability of four convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, DenseNet121, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and VGG16, for grape leaf disease classification across four classes of Black Rot, Esca (Black Measles), Leaf Blight, and Healthy. In addition to the standard performance metrics, we include external validation using an independent Kaggle dataset (9,027 images) to assess true generalizability, complementing the primary PlantVillage dataset (3,251 images). Results indicate that split ratio significantly affects model performance, with DenseNet121 showing outstanding stability across all splits and superior external test accuracy (up to 99.6%), while InceptionV3 demonstrates extreme instability, and ResNet50 shows noticeable variation. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) via gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) reveals that DenseNet121 and ResNet50 focus on pathologically significant leaf regions rather than spurious background correlations. This study offers a framework for assessing DL models in agriculture, highlighting that no single split ratio universally optimizes performance and emphasizing external validation for deploying trustworthy solutions.
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

The findings inform public health actions to combat measles resurgence and reinforce the role of vaccination in preventing transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the lessons learned from the West Texas measles outbreak regarding public health leadership and response strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary on the West Texas measles outbreak, which occurred in 2026, and focuses on public health leadership and management practices during the event.
analysis.methods: The methods involved a retrospective analysis of public health leadership strategies and outcomes during the West Texas measles outbreak, including case management, communication protocols, and community engagement.
analysis.main_results: The commentary highlights the importance of coordinated leadership, rapid response, and community engagement in mitigating the spread of measles during the outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a case study demonstrating the critical role of effective public health leadership in managing infectious disease outbreaks, offering novel insights into leadership practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health leadership training and preparedness for future outbreaks, emphasizing the need for proactive and collaborative strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a commentary and does not include quantitative data, which limits the strength of the evidence but provides valuable qualitative insights.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary reflects on the West Texas measles outbreak of 2026, emphasizing the importance of public health leadership in managing infectious disease crises. The study outlines the challenges faced during the outbreak and highlights the need for coordinated, rapid, and community-focused responses. While the analysis is qualitative and lacks quantitative data, it offers novel insights into leadership practices that can inform future outbreak management. The findings suggest that effective leadership is crucial for controlling measles outbreaks and improving public health preparedness. The study's limitations include its reliance on a narrative rather than empirical data, which affects the strength of the evidence but does not diminish its value as a case study.

title: Measles Vaccine Boosters in Immunocompromised Adults to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality From Acute Measles Infection: A Scoping Review

source_records.title: Measles Vaccine Boosters in Immunocompromised Adults to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality From Acute Measles Infection: A Scoping Review
Measles Vaccine Boosters in Immunocompromised Adults to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality From Acute Measles Infection: A Scoping Review
Measles Vaccine Boosters in Immunocompromised Adults to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality From Acute Measles Infection: A Scoping Review

full_text: Measles is a highly contagious viral illness associated with significant global mortality, despite the availability of an effective vaccine. As vaccine hesitancy continues to increase following the COVID-19 pandemic, combined with a lack of measles-specific antiviral agents, the risk of outbreaks and epidemics remains elevated. Immunocompromised individuals have a higher risk of serious complications from measles, especially because the live-attenuated measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine may be contraindicated in severely immunocompromised patients. As such, these individuals depend on herd immunity. This scoping review aims to identify the potential need for a measles booster dose among immunocompromised adults in the United States by providing an overview of current vaccine indications and outcomes. EMBASE, Web of Science, and Ovid MEDLINE were searched using search terms specific to measles booster doses and immunocompromised adults. In total, 2,335 articles were imported to Rayyan, and after a two-tiered review, seven articles met the full inclusion criteria. The results revealed that individuals with chronic immunocompromising illnesses were often not fully protected against measles, leaving them vulnerable to infection. The findings from this review suggest that clinicians may consider a booster dose of vaccine for immunocompromised individuals to help restore their protection against measles. Meanwhile, further research utilizing larger sample sizes and diverse patient populations is warranted based on these findings. We believe that additional studies should aim to clarify current guidelines to improve the care of immunocompromised patients who may be exposed to measles. ConclusionsThe results of this scoping review emphasized the need for future studies to support clear guidelines and policies regarding measles serologic screening and the administration of MMRV booster doses among immunocompromised individuals. This scoping review assessed the existing literature on measles immunity among individuals with immunocompromising conditions following vaccination. Specifically, there is an increasing need for further research to provide evidence to inform guidelines on the safety and use of booster vaccination in this population. Future studies should aim to include larger sample sizes and more diverse patient populations, encompassing a variety of immunocompromising conditions. Additionally, future studies should investigate the optimal timing of measles vaccine administration. This also underscores the importance of understanding the vaccine's safety profile across different immunocompromised states. Introduction and backgroundMeasles cases, despite the availability of an effective vaccine, spiked worldwide during 2017, resulting in the death of 110,000 individuals. Increased mortality was seen among both children and immunocompromised individuals [1]. Control efforts in the United States (U.S.) have been relatively ineffective at reducing measles cases, despite the declaration of measles elimination in 2000. Cases of measles in the U.S. continued to rise during 2024 [2,3]. Combined with the virus’s ability to be both immunosuppressive and erase the immune system’s memory of other pathogens, measles has the potential to negatively impact both immunocompromised and immunocompetent individuals [4]. Before vaccinations were available in 1963, the U.S. experienced four million cases and 450 deaths, as compared with current estimates of 20 million new cases and 100,000 deaths worldwide annually [2]. With the rapid introduction of the measles vaccine in the U.S. and the gradual introduction in Great Britain and other European countries, the prevalence of the disease declined from a common disease to a rarity [5]. Without a vaccine, measles epidemics would be expected to occur every two to five years, costing the U.S. $3.6 billion annually [1]. The potential for epidemics amid increased patient vaccine refusal and the lack of specific antiviral treatments highlight the importance of robust individual immunity to the measles virus [1,4,6,7].To eradicate measles in the U.S., mass vaccination is instrumental in lowering disease burden [8]. Long-lasting vaccine-induced immunity appears to be the best possible defense against measles, and severe immunosuppression is a contraindication for the live attenuated measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine and the measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella (MMRV) vaccine. As such, these populations depend on herd immunity for protection [9]. In those with previously compromised immune systems, such as children and adults who have been cured of cancer, a more rapid decline in measles antibodies has been found, indicating a potential need for repeat vaccinations beyond the initial two-dose regimen [9]. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a measles booster dose among immunocompromised individuals aged 21 years and older who were eligible for vaccination in the U.S.Understanding the pathophysiology of measles infection is important for understanding the need to prevent the disease through vaccination. The measles virus is a negative-sense, single-stranded ribonucleic acid virus that is transmitted via the respiratory route [3,10]. It is highly infectious, with 94% of the population requiring vaccination to achieve herd immunity [11]. Most patients infected with the virus are children, with a median age of nine years. Additionally, over 90% of patients infected with measles are unvaccinated [12]. Measles enters the body through the respiratory tract [3,13]. The measles virus targets respiratory tract dendritic cells and migrates to the lymphatic system, where the infection spreads throughout the body [1]. The incubation period is approximately 10 days. Fever and rash start to appear after approximately 14 days [1]. Cough and Koplik spots are characteristic features of measles infection [1]. Modified measles is a notably milder and less contagious variant of the disease that can occur among patients who have been vaccinated or previously infected [8].Measles vaccinations have drastically reduced the number of annual cases [2]. Cases and deaths within the U.S. have declined from an annual count of 535,600 to 142,300 between 2001 and 2018, respectively [8]. Severe complications, including hyponatremia, pneumonia, and death, are notably higher among hospitalized patients [14]. Supportive care is the prevailing approach to managing measles, as there is no specific U.S. Food and Drug Administration-approved treatment [15]. As such, vaccination has been vital to eradicating this disease [10].Measles is currently on the rise again in the U.S. [2,16]. Despite the existence of an effective vaccine, low vaccination rates in the U.S. are contributing to this increase [12]. This is despite evidence that the adverse effects of the MMRV are rare [17]. This trend is especially troublesome for immunocompromised patients, as they can progress to develop life-threatening complications, including but not limited to pneumonitis and encephalitis [18]. While most current U.S. literature on measles focuses on risks in the pediatric population, individuals aged 21 years and older who are immunocompromised in the U.S. face increased risk of contracting the virus as well. Immunocompromised individuals experience a more rapid decline in measles antibody levels after vaccination than immunocompetent individuals [9]. Increased secondary MMRV failure has been attributed in a significant number of U.S. cases to waning vaccine immunity, which could further increase the risk of measles infection among immunocompromised individuals [19].Measles infection in immunocompromised adults is a serious concern due to the lack of antiviral treatments and the increased risk of severe complications [15]. Because a 95% herd immunity threshold is needed to protect a population from measles, the measles booster could benefit not only immunocompromised individuals but also the population at large [20]. Given the current literature on measles and the annual increase in cases, there is a lack of information on the efficacy of a measles booster dose among immunocompromised individuals aged 21 years and older in the U.S. Given the increased risk of immunocompromised adults contracting measles due to declining herd immunity in the U.S., we conducted a scoping review to assess the potential need for immunization protocols to protect this vulnerable population. ReviewInclusion and exclusion criteriaFor our inclusion criteria, we included articles published between 2015 and 2025. U.S.-only publications were included; English-language-only articles were included. Cohort, case-control, and randomized controlled trials were included. Studies with adults aged 21 years and older were included, and the study population must consist of patients with an immunocompromising disease in the experimental group. Each study population was limited to a single immunocompromising disease being evaluated (i.e., one study cannot include both irritable bowel syndrome and diabetes, but it can include either one or the other). These criteria were intended to narrow the number of studies to allow a close examination of the most relevant studies for potential directions of future research on vaccines for adults in the U.S.For our exclusion criteria, case reports, expert opinions, or other opinion pieces were excluded. Additionally, scoping and systematic reviews were excluded, as were conference abstracts for which the full text could not be obtained. When going through the searches in Rayyan (Cambridge, MA, USA), we included exclusion labels, such as a + (positive) label for an exclusion criterion or a − (negative) label for an inclusion criterion, as the reason we did not include the article. All search results were imported into Rayyan using compatible formats. Duplicate records were removed prior to screening. Study selection was conducted in two tiers, followed by further critical appraisal of studies selected for inclusion in Tier-II.First, for Tier-I (title and abstract screening), review authors #1 and #2 screened titles and abstracts against the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Each record was marked as include, exclude, or maybe. Custom exclusion labels, in accordance with our inclusion and exclusion criteria (e.g., irrelevant population, incorrect study design), were applied to ensure consistency. Disagreements were flagged by Rayyan and resolved by a tiebreaker from review author #3, with brief reasons for exclusion provided for the abstracts we excluded. Second, for Tier-II (full-text screening), articles marked as "include" or "maybe" in Tier I underwent a more in-depth review by authors #1 and #2 to confirm their eligibility for data synthesis. Reviewers marked each text for exclusion or inclusion based on our criteria (outlined above). Any disagreements were resolved by author #3. The final set of included studies for synthesis in our review paper was exported from Rayyan to Excel (Microsoft Corp., Redmond, WA, USA) to create a data summary table. The Tier II articles also underwent critical appraisal using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal checklists. Then, a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) flow diagram was used to document the number of records identified, screened, excluded, and included in the final synthesis in an easy-to-digest format for inclusion in this scoping review [21].Data extraction and synthesisData extraction was conducted to organize data for a structured summary table in Excel after study selection was completed in Rayyan, in accordance with the inclusion and exclusion criteria for our population. The table divided parts of the articles into easily comparable fragments. The extracted variables included the author and year, the study's aim, the study population, the study methods, and the results and conclusions. We used this organization to identify patterns and trends in the articles we included and to synthesize the ideas found in those papers into an understandable narrative. The final extraction table is presented alongside the paper's review and synthesis to demonstrate compliance with JBI standards. The synthesis of our review aimed to identify trends, knowledge gaps, and questions for future research.Critical appraisalA critical appraisal of the studies gathered was conducted following the Tier II review to ensure our review was based on studies that contained reliable evidence. The JBI Critical Appraisal tools were used to systematically classify the final articles as high, moderate, or low quality [22]. A different checklist was used for each type of study design. Six reviewers assessed study design quality, bias/validity, methodological clarity, and transparency using the JBI checklists. Consensus on each article was reached by performing the JBI critical appraisal with multiple reviewers and comparing results.The JBI appraisal process was used to identify low-quality studies and to indicate whether a study was high, moderate, or low quality, based on responses from multiple collaborators, to determine whether it was of sufficient quality to be included in our final data synthesis.To accurately represent our data, we had to ensure that our articles were high-quality and scientifically sound. Papers with low validity could alter our data analysis and lead to misrepresentation. Studies, including those we selected for our scoping review, underwent a critical appraisal to assess the extent to which they had considered potential bias in their design, conduct, or analysis. Critical appraisal tools facilitate this evaluation. We used the JBI critical appraisal tool checklists to evaluate the articles identified as relevant to our study in our Tier-II review. We selected seven articles through our Tier-II review, and each article was assigned to one author for in-depth review using the appropriate JBI checklist based on the study's methodology. The studies assessed were categorized into three risk levels based on the percentage of questions answered positively in the JBI checklist. Scores below 50% indicated high risk, scores between 50% and 70% indicated moderate risk, and scores above 70% indicated low risk. All seven articles assessed scored above 70% in the JBI criteria and were included in our review. The relevance and quality of each study were thoroughly discussed to select the final articles for the review, and all seven were included.MethodsThis scoping review was conducted using the JBI methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. This scoping review examined adults aged 21 years or older with immunocompromising diseases, including but not limited to cancers, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), transplantation, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), Crohn’s disease, rheumatologic diseases, and diabetes. Only populations within the U.S. were examined.The inclusion criteria for this review, outlined above, included U.S.-only publications in English, published between 2015 and 2025. Other criteria included research studies using cohort, case-control, and randomized controlled designs. Manuscripts excluded from this analysis were case reports, expert opinions or other opinion pieces, scoping reviews, and systematic reviews. We also did not include conference abstracts for which we could not find the full text.The objective of this scoping review was to assess whether there is a need for a measles booster vaccine among immunocompromised adults in the U.S. This review analyzed current indications and outcomes for measles vaccination and booster dosing in this population.Eligibility criteriaResearch studies were included in the review if they involved immunocompromised adults aged 21 years or older in the U.S. and reported measles immunity or seroprevalence or demonstrated an immune response to measles vaccines. Studies that were published between 2015 and 2025 were considered for review. To narrow our study set to the most relevant articles, we established inclusion and exclusion criteria (as outlined above).Search strategyOur scoping review systematically searched the literature using Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science with Boolean operators (AND, OR, *) and search terms related to measles booster doses and immunocompromised adults. Terms such as “booster dose”, “measles mumps rubella”, “immunocompromised”, and "autoimmune" were also searched. The tables below provide an overview of the results by search term for each database queried (see Appendices).Authors #6-#10 conducted a literature search on the epidemiology/prevalence, pathophysiology, morbidity and mortality, treatment, and prevention of measles. Each author was responsible for locating four unique articles based on their search topic. The databases used are listed in our appendix below: Ovid MEDLINE, Web of Science, and EMBASE. The search findings were inserted into EndNote and screened for duplicates. One duplicate was identified, so author #7 located an additional article to use for the background section.A total of 2,335 references were imported to Rayyan. Duplicate articles were removed before the screening. Authors #1 and #2 independently conducted a blind Tier I review of the titles and abstracts of 1,226 articles. After authors #1 and #2's decisions, the blind review was lifted, and author #3 served as a tiebreaker for any disputed articles. After the Tier I screen, 1,205 articles were excluded for failing to meet the inclusion criteria. Twenty-two articles were initially approved. One article was excluded after confirming it did not meet the initial inclusion criteria of being written in English. Authors #4-#10, excluding author #5, collected the full text for 20 articles. full_text_excerpt: This scoping review aims to identify the potential need for a measles booster dose among immunocompromised adults in the United States by providing an overview of current vaccine indications and outcomes. In total, 2,335 articles were imported to Rayyan, and after a two-tiered review, seven articles met the full inclusion criteria. The results revealed that individuals with chronic immunocompromising illnesses were often not fully protected against measles, leaving them vulnerable to infection. The findings from this review suggest that clinicians may consider a booster dose of vaccine for immunocompromised individuals to help restore their protection against measles. Meanwhile, further research utilizing larger sample sizes and diverse patient populations is warranted based on these findings. ConclusionsThe results of this scoping review emphasized the need for future studies to support clear guidelines and policies regarding measles serologic screening and the administration of MMRV booster doses among immunocompromised individuals. This scoping review assessed the existing literature on measles immunity among individuals with immunocompromising conditions following vaccination. Measles is a highly contagious viral illness associated with significant global mortality, despite the availability of an effective vaccine. As vaccine hesitancy continues to increase following the COVID-19 pandemic, combined with a lack of measles-specific antiviral agents, the risk of outbreaks and epidemics remains elevated.
